body_markdown:
Agentic AI is turning one-way campaigns into ongoing, multi-step dialogues between people, brands and machines. At the same time, customers still expect brands to understand them as humans. That tension is the premise of Grow with Braze Bangkok 2026, with the umbrella theme of “AI is the connection catalyst.”


On 3 November, more than 170 marketers across CRM, marketing, data, and digital gathered at Andaz One Bangkok to test that idea in practice.


## Setting the scene


Shahid Nizami, VP of APAC and GCC at Braze, opened the event by framing the challenge clearly: In 2026, AI agents can search, decide, and act on behalf of consumers, turning one-way campaigns into multi-step dialogues between people, brands, and machines. The brands that will lead in this region are those that balance machine-driven speed and scale with genuine human nuance.


He closed the first session by introducing fresh insights from forge further emphasizing on Braze commitment to greater customer engagement.


## Customer spotlight: TrueMoney moves from messages to experiences


Benjamaporn Deebuk (Fern), Head of Growth Communication at TrueMoney, summed up the challenge by explaining that in one app, every customer arrives with a different need, intent, and context—whether paying a bill, scanning a QR code, topping up a phone, or shopping.


TrueMoney's answer is a system that learns. Over 200 models, covering touchpoint, service, lifestage and campaign mechanics, feed a reinforcement learning model that chooses the next best action. It selects the message, the channel, and the timing. The slides framed this as a shift from predicting who may act to deciding what experience should come next. Signals inform a decision, Braze delivers the journey, the customer's response flows back, and the loop learns.


The headline number was a 167% incremental uplift in click-through rate, with an upward trend since 2024 that reinforced the team's belief in personalized experiences. Today the approach runs through push and inbox. A splash page and discovery shelves are planned for November 2026, in service of an app customers want to open every day.


**The takeaway: TrueMoney is no longer optimizing a message. It is deciding an experience.**


## Humanizing conversations, building loyalty with POINT X and Merkle


An insightful panel session moderated by Kao Sutthitham, Thailand Enterprise Lead at Braze, joined by Napat Ruchdaponkul (Puhkao), Marketing Specialist at POINT X, and Thanoos Kerdlaup (Nuke), General Manager at Merkle Thailand.


POINT X brought three examples: A new loyalty platform concept, AI product recommendations through Content Cards, and a free-points Halloween campaign that used an in-app message to lead members to a landing page. Points themselves can be spent via scan-to-pay and at online shops and delivery platforms.


Merkle made the case that loyalty programmes have not kept pace with changing behavior and expectations. Only 25% of consumers feel personalization is delivered consistently, 60–70% of the customer data brands collect goes unused. Merkle’s Modern CRM framework took the same step for the whole system. It moved the focus from optimizing products, channels and separate campaigns to optimizing relationships and connected conversations. That meant bringing loyalty, messaging, and promotions together and tying them to paid media.


Merkle also showed a customer case study with a 5X increase in loyalty and CRM database in under eight months, and a 19.5% lift in purchase frequency from one promotion.


**The takeaway: Loyalty isn't the experience, it's what makes the experience work.**


## Braze spotlight: Brief it. Guard it. Grow it


Auzani Ridzwan, Lead Solutions Consultant, and Kevin Hu, AI Solutions Consultant, followed one customer, Ploy, through three live demos.


The verbs are the story. Marketers brief, guard, and grow, while the system builds, checks, and optimizes. The session closed on three business outcomes: More revenue, better compliance, and less manual work.


## Agents at work: How AI is rewiring the way teams operate


The final session of the event was moderated by Sarah Rouwendal, Senior Customer Success Manager at Braze. She was joined by Varis Shnatepaporn, Executive Vice President at JobTopGun, and Woradech (Birdie) Kamlangmuang, Head of Marketing at DDproperty who presented two paths: An agent built inside Braze and your own AI connected to Braze through its MCP server.


**The week has changed.** Varis described a team that once set up campaigns through the interface and configured templates and connected content. Now planning, email and notification builds, QA, creative variations, measurement and journey analysis have largely gone to agents, with people making creative decisions, connecting the dots and orchestrating.


Birdie described less time collecting information and more time interpreting it, and pointed to PropertyGuru’s Braze Assistant, tested in Singapore and Malaysia, which lets marketers ask about campaign performance in natural language. His caution was that AI can help do the work, but it doesn't automatically know which work matters most.


For JobTopGun, **foundations are first, and skills follow** . JobTopGun's agents rely on a data warehouse, product analytics, a centralized customer profile, and standard event tracking and sanitization across Braze and internal systems while employers are asking for critical thinking, problem solving, multi-disciplinary skills, and human skills like communication and negotiation.


**Timing beats volume.** Birdies shares that PropertyGuru Group's Singapore team used Braze's native AI Agent to time app-review requests.


In testing, asking after a positive experience produced roughly twice the click-through rate of asking at the start of an enquiry. Yet better timing alone didn't improve overall app ratings, product experience still matters. AI helps understand the context, Braze helps act at the right moment, and people remain accountable. At JobTopGun, AI planned a Canvas telling candidates they had appeared in recruiters' searches, to drive resume updates and then applications, and Claude routines summarized daily results.


**The line.** Having data, Birdie said, doesn't give AI permission to use it for any purpose. PropertyGuru Group's MCP testing surfaced real challenges with data retrieval, API limitations and how results are presented, so validation, permissions and human oversight come before anything customer-facing goes live. On customers' own AI assistants, Varis urged optimizing for AI and bots as well as people. Birdie noted that no one knows exactly how fast behavior will change, but trustworthy information will only become more valuable.


**The takeaway: Varis said start small, build and iterate. Birdie said start with the business problem, and judge AI by whether it helps people make better decisions, not by how much it automates.**


## Key takeaways


**1. The foundations decide what AI can do next.** Merkle's first principle, connecting identity, data and signals, and JobTopGun's warehouse and clean events are the same lesson.


**2. The next experience beats the next send.** TrueMoney's learning loop and PropertyGuru's deferred task are both bets on timing.


**3. Accountability doesn't automate.** Grow with Braze Asia called responsible AI a growth strategy; Bangkok's practitioners showed what that actually looks like day to day.
